violated_invariant: A DVM pool's init() must only be callable once, so its token pair and maintainer cannot be replaced after deployment.
rationale: Inside DVMFlashLoanCall the PoC calls dvm.init() again on a live pool and swaps the base/quote tokens for attacker tokens, so the flash-loan repayment check runs against the fake tokens and the real wCRES/USDT are kept. The DVM (0x051ebd...) has no recovered source, so the function names come from the PoC interface. None of the candidates with source (wCRES token, a maintainer proxy, FeeRateModel) holds the defect, and the DHL label 'Flashloan Attack' names the mechanism, not the root cause.

violated_invariant: Only the deploying pool may initialize the NFT contract and become its owner; init() must not be callable by anyone afterwards.
rationale: The PoC comment and code show a public init() with no caller restriction that hands ownership to msg.sender; the attacker then burns and re-mints deposit NFT #1 to themselves. No source was recovered for 0xf0b7..., so the file and function names are guesses taken from the PoC. Impact is set to 'other' (deposit-NFT ownership hijack) and in_scope is low-certainty, because I could not confirm a realized USD loss. The DHL label 'Access control' is a fair parent, but unprotected init is the more specific root cause.

violated_invariant: Cross-chain messages relayed by EthCrossChainManager must never be able to call privileged functions on EthCrossChainData, which owns the keeper key set.
rationale: The PoC sends a cross-chain tx whose toContract is EthCrossChainData and whose method string 'f1121318093' hashes to the selector of putCurEpochConPubKeyBytes(bytes). The manager is EthCrossChainData's owner, so it passes onlyOwner and replaces the keeper key. The defect is in EthCrossChainManager (0x838bf9..., no recovered source): it lets any target and any method name build the call. EthCrossChainData and LockProxy have source but are only affected, and none of their Slither findings (e.g. arbitrary-send-eth in LockProxy) describe this flaw.

off_chain_reason: No realized loss: the PoC forks block 13038771 (~Aug 2021) and reproduces the msg.value-in-batch bug, which was found and rescued by a whitehat; the CSV loss field says all funds were returned.
violated_invariant: The ETH sent with a transaction (msg.value) must be credited once, not once per delegatecall inside batch().
rationale: The PoC calls DutchAuction.batch() with five copies of commitEth, so msg.value is counted five times because batch delegatecalls back into the contract. The real defect is msg.value reuse in the delegatecall batch loop (business logic), not missing input validation as the DHL label says. No source was recovered for the auction. I marked it out of scope as no real loss; the reviewer should check whether the 2021-09-16 date actually points to the separate MISO frontend supply-chain incident, which would also be out of scope.

violated_invariant: vVISR shares may only be minted for VISR the contract actually received.
rationale: RewardsHypervisor.deposit trusts a caller-supplied 'from' contract. It only checks IVisor(from).owner()==msg.sender, calls from.delegatedTransferERC20, and then mints shares without checking that its VISR balance went up. The PoC's contract returns itself as owner and has an empty delegatedTransferERC20, so it gets 1e26 shares for free. There is no reentrant call, so I think the DHL 'Reentrancy' label is wrong. Slither's arbitrary-send-erc20 (index 0) flags the other branch (safeTransferFrom with an arbitrary from), not the exploited path.

violated_invariant: ACOWriter must never make calls with its own identity to arbitrary targets, because users have given it standing ERC20 approvals.
rationale: write() takes a user-controlled exchangeAddress and exchangeData, and _sellACOTokens runs _exchange.call(exchangeData) without any allowlist. The PoC sets exchangeAddress=USDC and the data to transferFrom(victim 0xcb3203..., attacker, balance), which spends the victim's approval to ACOWriter. Its mock acoToken gets it past the earlier steps. Slither's low-level-calls (index 4) points at that exact line, but it is only an informational note about using a low-level call and does not describe the arbitrary-target weakness, so I left it out.

violated_invariant: An FNFT id's deposit-per-unit config must not change while that id is being minted, and getNextId() must account for an id mid-mint.
rationale: FNFTHandler.mint calls _mint, which triggers the onERC1155Received callback, before it increments fnftsCreated. In that callback the PoC reenters depositAdditionalToFNFT(fnftId,1e18,1). Its createNewSeries path uses getNextId(), which still equals the id being minted (360,000 units at depositAmount 0), so that id's per-unit value is raised to 1e18 and withdrawFNFT drains RENA. The flash swap only supplies working capital. Slither finding 46 (reentrancy-benign: FNFTHandler.mint writes fnftsCreated after the ERC1155 callback) describes exactly this ordering, though it rates it Low. FNFTHandler is a separately deployed contract whose address I have not verified, so it is not listed as a victim.

violated_invariant: Voting power used to pass and execute a proposal must not be acquirable and usable within a single transaction.
rationale: The PoC proposes a malicious BIP, warps one day, flash-borrows about $1B, deposits it into the Silo for instant Stalk, and calls emergencyCommit. The 2/3 supermajority is checked against power that counts immediately, and the BIP's init then drains the Silo. The defect is in GovernanceFacet behind the Diamond proxy (0xc1e088...). The recovered Diamond sources only contain the cut, loupe and ownership facets, so the defect code was not available to Slither, and no finding applies. The Bean token and Curve pools are only affected or used as tools.

violated_invariant: An account's borrow balance must be recorded before ETH is sent out, so collateral cannot be withdrawn while a borrow is outstanding.
rationale: borrowFresh calls doTransferOut (a raw ETH call in CEther) before it writes accountBorrows. The PoC's receive() reenters Comptroller.exitMarket, which has no reentrancy guard, sees zero debt, and frees the fUSDC collateral, which is then redeemed. The two victims are delegator/Unitroller proxies, and the defect lives in their CEtherDelegate and Comptroller implementations (sources included in the candidate's files). Slither finding 430 (reentrancy-no-eth on borrowFresh) flags accountBorrows written after external calls and readable cross-function through borrowBalanceStoredInternal. That is the exploited state, though it cites the comptroller calls rather than the ETH transfer, so treat it as borderline.

violated_invariant: Proxy-admin storage must not overlap the logic contract's Initializable flags, so initialize() stays one-shot behind the proxy.
rationale: AudiusAdminUpgradeabilityProxy declares proxyAdmin in slot 0. The pre-exploit logic (Staking.sol, DelegateManagerV2.sol) keeps Initializable's initialized/initializing bools in that same slot, so the admin address bytes make the initializer check pass again. The PoC re-initializes Governance, Staking and DelegateManager, delegates fake stake, then submits and executes a proposal that transfers AUDIO. Caution: the Governance logic candidate 0x1c91af... was deployed at block 15203848, after the fork block 15201793, and its Initializable already has the proxyAdmin fix. So it is the post-incident implementation, not the exploited code. Slither has no cross-contract storage-collision finding here.

violated_invariant: A DAO-module proposal must not execute Safe transactions unless the community has had a meaningful, bonded chance to dispute it.
rationale: Anyone can call addProposal. executeProposalWithIndex only needs the Reality.eth answer to be 1, a bond of at least minimumBond (0 disables the check), and the cooldown to have passed. The PoC answers its own question on Realitio, waits, then executes txs that mint 1e14 RNBW and hand PrimaryBridge/LPOP ownership to the attacker. This is a governance-design and configuration weakness (bond, cooldown, no monitoring or arbitrator), not a coding bug, and no Slither finding (event or timestamp notes) describes it. The realized USD loss looks small, so the reviewer may want to confirm in_scope.

violated_invariant: Only an authorized minter can create new token supply.
rationale: Token.sol defines mint() as public with no modifier, minting 1e17 units to msg.sender. The PoC calls mint() once and sells the result into the UERII/USDC Uniswap V3 pool. The only Slither hit on mint is too-many-digits, which does not describe the missing check.

violated_invariant: Redeeming shares returns only the underlying those shares are worth.
rationale: The candidate is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy whose OpenZeppelin source is not the defect. The bug sits in the unrecovered ENF vault implementation: public analyses say an upgrade changed the storage layout, so redeem() read collided state and paid out far more USDC than the shares were worth. The PoC calls only redeem(676562, exploiter). All Slither findings are generic proxy noise.

violated_invariant: yUSDT's pool valuation counts only assets it can redeem as USDT, so its share price cannot be collapsed to near zero.
rationale: The legacy yUSDT vault was misconfigured to use bZx iUSDC instead of iUSDT as its Fulcrum provider. The attacker donated iUSDC to raise the share price, withdrew, then called rebalance() to drive the pool to about 1 wei. A 10k-unit deposit then minted a huge number of yUSDT, which was dumped into the Curve y pool. None of the candidates is the victim (they are Aave V1 debtor addresses), and there is no source. The other label fits a misconfiguration; business_logic is a reasonable alternative.

violated_invariant: No caller can move token balances out of an arbitrary address, such as the LP pair.
rationale: VINU.sol's addLiquidityETH is external with no access check and takes devaddr from the caller. It moves 80% of devaddr's balance into the token contract and then calls a caller-supplied router. The PoC passes the Uniswap pair as devaddr four times, calls sync() and sells into the gutted reserves. The DHL label 'Price Manipulation' describes the mechanism, not the root cause. unused-return (11/12) only flags ignored return values.

violated_invariant: Omnipool deposits and withdrawals must not execute against Curve pools at manipulated, imbalanced prices.
rationale: The PoC repeatedly unbalances the crvUSD/USDT and crvUSD/USDC Curve pools, then deposits to and withdraws from the Omnipool, which forwards funds through the curveHandler. The pool values holdings with oracle prices but executes against the skewed pools without a tight imbalance or slippage guard, so the attacker sandwiches it. The exact failing check, likely in the unrecovered CurveHandler or the oracle imbalance threshold, is unconfirmed. price_oracle_trust is the plausible alternative. None of the many reentrancy and unused-return findings describes this.

violated_invariant: A withdrawal debits the balance of the account that authorised it, and balances cannot underflow.
rationale: No source was recovered. The PoC deposits 2 USDT, sets a zero-length alt lock from a helper, and calls withdrawTokensWithAlt for the helper. The helper then withdraws the contract's whole balance. A public analysis says the function checked one account's balance but debited another, unchecked, which inflated the helper's balance.

violated_invariant: When a swap's price moves past a tick boundary, the tick must be crossed and active liquidity updated.
rationale: Kyber Elastic's SwapMath computes the amount needed to reach the next tick and the final price with inconsistent rounding. A carefully sized swap ends just past the boundary without the tick being treated as crossed, so liquidity is double-counted on the way back. The PoC sets up a narrow position and runs crafted swap amounts. The divide-before-multiply and incorrect-exp hits are in FullMath.mulDivFloor and are false positives, not this bug.

violated_invariant: collectInterest only calls approved staking contracts, and minted interest reflects real yield, not balance changes made during the call.
rationale: The PoC passes an attacker contract in _stakingContracts to GoodFundManager.collectInterest. The manager calls back into that contract's collectUBIInterest, which re-enters GDX.buy and inflates the cDAI the reserve counts as interest, so G$ is minted and sold for DAI. The candidate 0x0c6c… is an ERC1967Proxy and its source is OZ only; the implementation with the defect was not recovered. No Slither finding applies.

violated_invariant: redeem only releases assets against shares the caller owns and burns.
rationale: The PoC calls redeem(BUI.balanceOf(victim), attacker) from an account holding no shares and receives the contract's USDC, DAI, MATIC, AAVE, ENS, ZRX and UNI. The victim has no recovered source; the candidate SetToken (BUI) is affected, not defective. input_validation (no share-ownership check) is an equally defensible label.

violated_invariant: Only internal reward accounting can credit a player's stepIncome.
rationale: MainPool.sol's calcStepIncome(pid, value, pct) is public and credits stepIncome and totalSettled to any pid with caller-chosen values. The PoC joins the game from a constructor, which bypasses the extcodesize notContract check, credits itself and calls withdraw(). Slither's reentrancy and divide-before-multiply hits do not describe the missing access control.

violated_invariant: Collateral is valued at its true USD worth, with token decimals normalized correctly.
rationale: With 1 WETH of bWETH collateral the PoC borrows about 8.6k OHM, 913k USDC and 6.9 WBTC, far more than it should. Blueberry's post-mortem blames an oracle error, reportedly decimal handling, that overvalued the bWETH collateral. The oracle contract is not among the candidates, so the defect location is unverified. A reviewer may prefer price_oracle_trust or rounding_precision; the taxonomy has no decimal-scaling value.

violated_invariant: The aggregator only executes swap calls on approved DEX targets and never spends users' standing approvals for anyone else.
rationale: The PoC sends one crafted calldata blob to the Unizen proxy. Embedded in it is DMTR.transferFrom(victim, proxy, amount), which the aggregator executes, draining a user's approval. The candidate is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy with OZ source only; the implementation is unverified, so no source exists for the defect.

violated_invariant: initialize can run only once, and only the owner can upgrade the proxy.
rationale: The PoC calls initialize() to make itself owner, then upgradeToAndCall to its own implementation, whose withdraw sends the proxy's ETH. Public reports say a prior upgrade shifted storage so the initialized flag read as unset. That makes storage_collision a contributing cause, not only a never-initialized proxy. No source was recovered.

violated_invariant: Single-token liquidity removal pays out no more than the LP's pro-rata share.
rationale: removeLiquidity computes F=(1-R)^16 in 64-bit fixed point using truncating shifts. When LPamount is close to totalSupply, F rounds to 0 and the output equals the pool's entire balance of the chosen token. The PoC flash-loans, adds liquidity across all 16 tokens to own most of the supply, and removes it all as ETH. Slither produced no findings for DeFiPlaza.

violated_invariant: Router commands only call vetted swap targets and never spend third-party approvals.
rationale: The PoC calls execute() with command 0x12 and passes asdCRV as the swap target, with calldata transferFrom(victim, attacker, balance). The router executes this unvalidated call and spends the victim's approval. The candidate is an AMTransparentUpgradeableProxy; the Router implementation holding the defect was not recovered.

violated_invariant: A deposit's reward is paid once, not on every withdrawal.
rationale: withdraw() pays getPendingRewards(), which sums amount*rewardBps over every vested deposit and never records rewards already paid. Each withdraw(1) therefore pays the full reward again. The PoC deposits, waits 14 days and calls withdraw(1) 800 times. Slither's timestamp hits on these functions do not describe the double-claim.

violated_invariant: Protocol-owned reward swaps execute with bounded slippage that callers cannot override.
rationale: TokenRewards.sol's depositFromPairedLpToken is public and lets any caller set _slippageOverride; the PoC uses 999, i.e. 99.9%. The contract then swaps its own pOHM for PEAS with almost no minimum. The PoC skews the V3 pool with a flash swap, triggers the swap and unwinds. The DHL root cause price_oracle_trust is off: the TWAP is used, but the caller-controlled slippage defeats it. The divide-before-multiply and reentrancy findings on this function do not describe the issue.

violated_invariant: Borrowing is allowed only against collateral valued at a current, accurate price.
rationale: The PoC buys AMP with flash-loaned WETH, posts it as Kashi collateral and borrows USDC worth more than the AMP, then repays the loan and keeps 572 USDC. It never calls updateExchangeRate, so a stale or mispriced stored AMP exchange rate may explain the overvaluation, not manipulation; the buys only acquire collateral. The Kashi pair and its oracle have no recovered source, so the exact cause is unverified.

violated_invariant: After a branch shutdown, urgent redemptions do not pay redeemers more collateral than the debt they repay plus the intended bonus.
rationale: The PoC flash-loans USDT, buys USDaf and calls TroveManager.urgentRedemption on two chosen troves to receive scrvUSD from the ActivePool at a profit of about $4.2k. Liquity-v2-style urgent redemption with a bonus is a designed feature after shutdown. The loss may come from the shutdown price feed or bonus parameters rather than a code defect, and a reviewer may judge it out of scope. TroveManager source is not in the candidates; ActivePool only holds the collateral, and its Slither findings are unrelated.

violated_invariant: Funds move from `from` only with a valid permit signature or an approval granted for that purpose.
rationale: anySwapOutUnderlyingWithPermit calls permit() on the underlying of an attacker-supplied token and then transferFrom(from, token, amount). WETH has no permit but its fallback accepts the call, so the permit becomes a no-op. The router then spends the victim's existing max allowance into the attacker's fake token. Slither finding 0 (arbitrary-send-erc20-permit) names exactly this function and pattern.

violated_invariant: Rounding in swaps always favours the pool, so the invariant D and the BPT price cannot be pushed down by a series of swaps.
rationale: The PoC runs one long batchSwap of GIVEN_OUT swaps, with offline-computed amounts, that pushes token balances to tiny values. There, _upscale's mulDown on the scaling factor or rate loses precision against the pool. Each step underestimates the invariant, deflating the BPT price, and the attacker then exits. The LogExpMath divide-before-multiply and BasePool incorrect-return hits are unrelated false positives.

violated_invariant: Vault-owned USDC must not be swapped at an attacker-chosen pool price; swaps need a minimum-out bound and a trusted caller.
rationale: The PoC flash-borrows ~14M USDC from Morpho, dumps it into the USDC/WETH V3 pool to skew the price, then calls the vault's swapToWETH(100k USDC) directly from the attack contract and back-runs the pool to keep the difference. That only works if swapToWETH is callable by anyone and swaps at spot with no slippage bound, which matches the 'slippage' post-mortem title. The vault (0x6a06...) has no recovered source, so the function name comes from the PoC interface; Morpho, DexRouter, TokenApprove and the pool are tooling, not the defect.

violated_invariant: A signed VaultAuth must commit to every SwapInfo field (fromToken, toToken, amount, aggregator), not just the calldata bytes.
rationale: _validateAuthorization hashes only keccak256(swap.data) for each compound swap, so fromToken, toToken, amount and aggregator can be swapped out under a valid signature. executeSwap then calls forceApprove(fromToken, aggregator, amount) on the strategy, and the PoC sets fromToken to the gauge token, aggregator to its helper and amount to uint256.max, then pulls the strategy's balance with transferFrom. 0x5f0a... looks like the shared implementation behind the vault proxies (0x9c24/0x51b9/0x1d85, which have no source); the defect lives in this code. The PoC whitelists its own test signer, which stands in for the reused real signatures. No Slither finding describes the missing field coverage.

violated_invariant: The router may only pull tokens from a payer who started the current operation; standing ERC-20 approvals must not be spendable by third parties.
rationale: The PoC replaces the router's code with vm.etch, so it shows only the result: inside Core's lock/pay callbacks, WBTC is transferFrom'd out of a victim who had approved the router, 0.2 WBTC per lock, 85 times. Public write-ups say the router's payment callback never checked that the named payer started or agreed to the operation. The router (0x8ccb...) has no recovered source, so the defect can only be marked at contract level; Ekubo Core (0xe0e0...) is just the settlement layer, and none of its Slither findings apply. input_validation would also be a reasonable label.

violated_invariant: Every withdrawal paid by the rollup must be bound to public inputs that the verified proof actually constrains; total withdrawals must not exceed deposits.
rationale: Anyone can call escapeHatch while the block window is open. The PoC proofs encode rollupSize = 0, which validateMerkleRoots turns into numTxs = 1, and the verifier is called with rollupSize 0. processDepositsAndWithdrawals then pays publicOutput to an address with no deposit, draining all the ETH, DAI and renBTC. Reports blame a public-input binding gap between the processor and the TurboVerifier (0x48cb..., not in candidates, no source), so the exact defect line, and whether it sits in the processor or the verifier, is unconfirmed. The arbitrary-send and reentrancy findings on withdraw only describe the payout path.

violated_invariant: Calls the factory makes to the PositionManager as itself must be restricted to the intended pool-initialize and mint actions.
rationale: launch() is permissionless and passes caller-supplied initCalldata and modifyCalldata unchanged into PositionManager.multicall, with the factory as msg.sender. The PoC passes setApprovalForAll(attacker, true) as modifyCalldata, then burns the 7 LP NFTs the factory holds and takes both tokens. The PoolManager (0x0000...4444), which DHL lists as a victim, holds no defect, and Slither's arbitrary-send-eth on launch is about the dust refund, not this.

violated_invariant: A live contract registry's initializer must not be re-runnable, so only the legitimate manager can change the logic that item adapters delegatecall into.
rationale: The PoC calls initialize(1) and then acceptManager() on both registries with no privilege, becomes manager, and uses updateContract to make the adapter clones delegatecall its own transfer code. It then moves 54 items out of holders and melts them for 5.23M ENJ. Neither registry has recovered source; the only candidate with source is the ENJ token, which is not at fault. So the names here come from the PoC interface. The CSV victim_addresses is empty and should list the registries.

violated_invariant: A transfer of amount X must move exactly X token units; an amount that also parses as an NFT id must not move a whole 1e18 unit.
rationale: O404.transfer and transferFrom treat any valueOrId <= maxTotalSupplyERC721 (50) as an NFT id and move a full units (1e18) of ERC-20 with it. The PoC uses V3 flash plus id-path repayment so the pool owns the low ids, then runs exact-output swaps of `id` wei, where the pool's transfer pays out 1e18 per ~2 wei of WETH. The defect is in the token (0xd5c0...), not in the pool or the Balancer Vault that DHL lists as victims; the Vault only supplies the flash loan. Slither's erc721-interface hits are about return types, not this.

violated_invariant: Interest for an idle gap must accrue once at the rate in force during the gap, not again on every action in the block at a utilization the caller just set.
rationale: _checkFirstAction stores the full idle block gap (264,059 blocks) and freezes actionEXR on the block's first action. Per the PoC, getInterestAmount then applies that whole gap on every later same-block action at the current SIR, which comes from deposit and borrow totals the attacker sets with a Morpho flash loan. UsdtHandlerProxy (0x808c...) only delegatecalls into TokenHandler, so it is not the defect; the interest model (0x29ec...) is not among the candidates and its code is cited from the PoC header. No Slither finding covers this accrual logic.
